title.zh: 卷十一 志第一 禮樂一
title.raw: 卷十一 志第一 禮樂一 Volume 11 Treatises 1: Rites and Music 1

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 由三代而上，治出於一，而禮樂達于天下；

translations.literal: From the Three Dynasties upward, governance issued from one source, and rites and music reached throughout the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Before the Three Dynasties ended, government and ritual issued from a single source, and rites and music permeated the realm;

sentences.zh: 由三代而下，治出於二，而禮樂為虛名。

translations.literal: From the Three Dynasties downward, governance issued from two sources, and rites and music became empty names.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Dynasties, government split in two, and rites and music became mere names.

sentences.zh: 古者，宮室車輿以為居，衣裳冕弁以為服，尊爵俎豆以為器，金石絲竹以為樂，以適郊廟，以臨朝廷，以事神而治民。

translations.literal: In antiquity, palaces and carriages served as dwelling; robes, caps, and coronets served as dress; goblets, bells, and stands served as vessels; metal, stone, silk, and bamboo served as music—to attend suburban altars and ancestral temples, to preside at court, to serve the spirits and govern the people.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, palaces and carriages were one's home, garments and ceremonial caps one's dress, goblets and sacrificial stands one's vessels, and metal, stone, silk, and bamboo one's music—used at suburban altars and temples, at court, to serve the spirits and govern the people.

sentences.zh: 其歲時聚會以為朝覲、聘問，懽欣交接以為射鄉、食饗，合眾興事以為師田、學校，下至里閭田畝，吉凶哀樂，凡民之事，莫不一出於禮。

translations.literal: Their seasonal gatherings served as court audiences and diplomatic missions; joyful social exchanges served as archery fêtes and feasts; assembling the multitude for undertakings served as military hunts and schools—from village lanes and fields down to joy, sorrow, and music in the lives of common people, nothing among the people's affairs did not wholly issue from ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal gatherings became court audiences and embassies; festive gatherings became archery meets and banquets; mass assemblies became military hunts and schools. Down to village lanes and fields, through joy and grief and music in ordinary life—nothing in the people's affairs fell outside ritual.

sentences.zh: 由之以教其民為孝慈、友悌、忠信、仁義者，常不出於居處、動作、衣服、飲食之間。

translations.literal: Through these to teach the people filial piety, kindness, fraternity, loyalty, faith, benevolence, and righteousness—such teaching rarely departed from dwelling, movement, clothing, and food.
translations.idiomatic: Through these the people were taught filial piety, kindness, fraternity, loyalty, faith, benevolence, and righteousness—almost always within the bounds of daily dwelling, movement, dress, and food.

sentences.zh: 蓋其朝夕從事者，無非乎此也。

translations.literal: For what they pursued morning and evening was nothing but this.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening they pursued nothing but this.

sentences.zh: 此所謂治出於一，而禮樂達天下，使天下安習而行之，不知所以遷善遠罪而成俗也。

translations.literal: This is what is called governance issuing from one source, with rites and music reaching all under Heaven, causing all under Heaven to practice them securely and habitually, unaware how they turned toward goodness, shunned wrongdoing, and formed custom.
translations.idiomatic: This is governance from a single source, with rites and music reaching the world—so that all under Heaven practiced them securely, unaware how they turned toward goodness, shunned wrongdoing, and formed custom.

sentences.zh: 及三代已亡，遭秦變古，後之有天下者，自天子百官名號位序、國家制度、宮車服器一切用秦，其間雖有欲治之主，思所改作，不能超然遠復三代之上，而牽其時俗，稍即以損益，大抵安於苟簡而已。

translations.literal: When the Three Dynasties had perished and Qin transformed antiquity, those who afterward possessed the realm—from the Son of Heaven, officials' titles and ranks, state institutions, palaces, carriages, dress, and vessels—all used Qin models. Though there were rulers who wished to govern well and thought to reform, none could transcend their age and restore what lay above the Three Dynasties; pulled by contemporary custom, they made slight additions and subtractions, and for the most part rested content with what was crude and simple.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Dynasties had fallen and Qin overturned antiquity, every later holder of the realm—from the Son of Heaven through official titles, state institutions, palaces, carriages, dress, and vessels—followed Qin. Even rulers who wished to reform could not rise above their age to restore the Three Dynasties; tugged by contemporary custom, they made minor adjustments and mostly settled for what was crude and simple.

sentences.zh: 其朝夕從事，則以簿書、獄訟、兵食為急，曰：「此為政也，所以治民。

translations.literal: What they pursued morning and evening was registers, lawsuits, armies, and provisions as urgent matters, saying: "This is government; by it the people are governed.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening they busied themselves with registers, lawsuits, armies, and provisions, saying: "This is government; by it the people are governed.

sentences.zh: 」至於三代禮樂，具其名物而藏於有司，時出而用之郊廟、朝廷，曰：「此為禮也，所以教民。

translations.literal: " As for the rites and music of the Three Dynasties, their names and objects were fully listed and stored with the relevant offices, brought out at times for use at suburban altars and court, with the saying: "This is ritual; by it the people are taught.
translations.idiomatic: " The rites and music of the Three Dynasties were catalogued and kept by the relevant offices, brought out occasionally for suburban altars and court, with the saying: "This is ritual; by it the people are taught.

sentences.zh: 」此所謂治出於二，而禮樂為虛名。

translations.literal: " This is what is called governance issuing from two sources, and rites and music becoming empty names.
translations.idiomatic: " This is governance from two sources, with rites and music mere empty names.

sentences.zh: 故自漢以來，史官所記事物名數、降登揖讓、拜俛伏興之節，皆有司之事爾，所謂禮之末節也。

translations.literal: Therefore from Han onward, what historiographers recorded—names and numbers of things, ascending and descending, bowing and yielding, the protocols of bowing, prostrating, rising, and kneeling—were all matters for the relevant offices, the so-called minor protocols of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: From Han onward, what historiographers recorded—the names and numbers of things, ascending and descending, bowing and yielding, the protocols of bowing, prostrating, rising, and kneeling—were all the business of relevant offices, the so-called minor protocols of ritual.

sentences.zh: 然用之郊廟、朝廷，自搢紳、大夫從事其間者，皆莫能曉習，而天下之人至於老死未嘗見也，況欲識禮樂之盛，曉然諭其意而被其教化以成俗乎？

translations.literal: Yet when used at suburban altars and court, even gentry and grandees who took part in them could none master the practice; the people of the realm lived to old age without ever seeing them—how much less could they recognize the fullness of rites and music, clearly understand their meaning, and receive their transforming instruction to form custom?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when these were used at suburban altars and court, even gentry and grandees who took part could not master them; common people lived to old age without ever seeing them—how could they grasp the fullness of rites and music, understand their meaning, and receive their transforming instruction to form custom?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 習其器而不知其意，忘其本而存其末，又不能備具，所謂朝覲、聘問、射鄉、食饗、師田、學校、冠婚、喪葬之禮在者幾何？

translations.literal: Practicing the vessels without knowing their meaning, forgetting the root while keeping the branches, and unable to supply them fully—of the so-called rites of court audience, diplomatic mission, archery fête, feast, military hunt, school, capping, marriage, and burial, how many remained?
translations.idiomatic: They learned the vessels without knowing their meaning, kept the branches while forgetting the root, and could not supply them fully—of court audiences, embassies, archery fêtes, feasts, military hunts, schools, capping, marriage, and burial rites, how many remained?

sentences.zh: 自梁以來，始以其當時所行傅於周官五禮之名，各立一家之學。

translations.literal: From Liang onward, they first applied what was then practiced to the names of the Five Rites in the Offices of Zhou, each establishing a separate school of learning.
translations.idiomatic: From Liang onward, contemporary practice was first mapped onto the Five Rites of the Offices of Zhou, each school establishing its own tradition.

sentences.zh: 唐初，即用隋禮，至太宗時，中書令房玄齡、祕書監魏徵，與禮官、學士等因隋之禮，增以天子上陵、朝廟、養老、大射、講武、讀時令、納皇后、皇太子入學、太常行陵、合朔、陳兵太社等，為吉禮六十一篇，賓禮四篇，軍禮二十篇，嘉禮四十二篇，凶禮十一篇，是為貞觀禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang they immediately used Sui ritual. By Taizong's time, Chief Minister Fang Xuanling, Secretariat Director Wei Zheng, with ritual officials and academicians, building on Sui ritual, added such items as the Son of Heaven's tomb visits, temple audiences, nurturing the aged, great archery, military review, reading the seasons, receiving the empress, the crown prince entering school, the Director of Court Music visiting tombs, new moon, and displaying troops at the Grand Earth altar—making sixty-one sections of auspicious ritual, four of guest ritual, twenty of military ritual, forty-two of felicitous ritual, and eleven of inauspicious ritual: this was the Zhenguan Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Early Tang adopted Sui ritual outright. Under Taizong, Chief Minister Fang Xuanling and Secretariat Director Wei Zheng, with ritual officials and academicians, built on Sui ritual and added the Son of Heaven's tomb visits, temple audiences, nurturing the aged, great archery, military review, reading the seasons, receiving the empress, the crown prince entering school, the Director of Court Music visiting tombs, new moon, and displaying troops at the Grand Earth altar—sixty-one sections of auspicious ritual, four of guest ritual, twenty of military ritual, forty-two of felicitous ritual, and eleven of inauspicious ritual: the Zhenguan Ritual.

sentences.zh: 高宗又詔太尉長孫无忌、中書令杜正倫李義府、中書侍郎李友益、黃門侍郎劉祥道許圉師、太子賓客許敬宗、太常卿韋琨等增之為一百三十卷，是為顯慶禮。

translations.literal: Gaozong further ordered Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Chief Ministers Du Zhenglun and Li Yifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Youyi, Vice Directors of the Yellow Gate Liu Xiangdao and Xu Yushi, Guest of the Heir Apparent Xu Jingzong, Director of Court Music Wei Kun, and others to expand it to one hundred thirty scrolls: this was the Xianqing Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong further ordered Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Chief Ministers Du Zhenglun and Li Yifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Youyi, Vice Directors of the Yellow Gate Liu Xiangdao and Xu Yushi, Guest of the Heir Apparent Xu Jingzong, Director of Court Music Wei Kun, and others to expand it to one hundred thirty scrolls: the Xianqing Ritual.

sentences.zh: 其文雜以式令，而義府、敬宗方得幸，多希旨傅會。

translations.literal: Its text was mixed with statutes and orders; Yifu and Jingzong were then in favor and largely bent their work to please imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Its text was mixed with statutes and orders. Yifu and Jingzong were then in favor and largely bent their work to please imperial intent.

sentences.zh: 事既施行，議者皆以為非，上元三年，詔復用貞觀禮。

translations.literal: Once it was put into practice, critics all deemed it wrong; in the third year of Shangyuan, an edict restored use of the Zhenguan Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Once implemented, critics deemed it wrong; in the third year of Shangyuan, an edict restored the Zhenguan Ritual.

sentences.zh: 由是終高宗世，貞觀、顯慶二禮兼行。

translations.literal: Thus through the end of Gaozong's reign, the Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals were practiced together.
translations.idiomatic: Thus through the end of Gaozong's reign, the Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals were practiced together.

sentences.zh: 而有司臨事，遠引古義，與二禮參考增損之，無復定制。

translations.literal: Yet when offices faced affairs, they cited distant ancient principles and consulted both rituals for additions and subtractions, with no fixed standard thereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when offices faced affairs. they cited distant ancient principles and consulted both rituals for additions and subtractions, with no fixed standard thereafter.

sentences.zh: 武氏、中宗繼以亂敗，無可言者，博士掌禮，備官而已。

translations.literal: The Wu clan and Zhongzong followed with turmoil and ruin—nothing worth speaking of; doctors of ritual held ritual in name only, filling posts and nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu clan and Zhongzong followed with turmoil and ruin—nothing worth speaking of. doctors of ritual held ritual in name only, filling posts and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元十年，以國子司業韋縚為禮儀使，以掌五禮。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xuanzong's Kaiyuan reign, Wei Zong of the Directorate of Education was made Commissioner of Ritual Protocol to oversee the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xuanzong's Kaiyuan reign, Wei Zong of the Directorate of Education was made Commissioner of Ritual Protocol to oversee the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 十四年，通事舍人王喦上疏，請刪去禮記舊文而益以今事，詔付集賢院議。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Remonstrance Clerk Wang Yan memorialized, asking to delete old text from the Book of Rites and add present affairs; an edict referred it to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, Remonstrance Clerk Wang Yan memorialized, asking to delete old text from the Book of Rites and add present affairs. an edict referred it to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 學士張說以為禮記不刊之書，去聖久遠，不可改易，而唐貞觀顯慶禮，儀注前後不同，宜加折衷，以為唐禮。

translations.literal: Academician Zhang Yue held that the Book of Rites was an unalterable book, far from the sages and not to be changed, while Tang's Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals had ritual directions that differed before and after and should be harmonized into Tang ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Zhang Yue held that the Book of Rites was an unalterable book. far from the sages and not to be changed, while Tang's Zhenguan and Xianqing rituals had ritual directions that differed before and after and should be harmonized into Tang ritual.

sentences.zh: 乃詔集賢院學士右散騎常侍徐堅、左拾遺李銳及太常博士施敬本撰述，歷年未就而銳卒，蕭嵩代銳為學士，奏起居舍人王仲丘撰定，為一百五十卷，是為大唐開元禮。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Academy academicians Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Xu Jian, Left Reminder Li Rui, and Court Music Doctor Shi Jingben to compile; years passed without completion and Rui died; Xiao Song replaced Rui as academician and memorialized that Diarist Wang Zhongqiu complete the work—in one hundred fifty scrolls: this was the Great Tang Kaiyuan Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Academy academicians Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Xu Jian, Left Reminder Li Rui, and Court Music Doctor Shi Jingben to compile; years passed without completion and Rui died; Xiao Song replaced Rui as academician and memorialized that Diarist Wang Zhongqiu complete the work—in one hundred fifty scrolls: the Great Tang Kaiyuan Ritual.

sentences.zh: 由是，唐之五禮之文始備，而後世用之，雖時小有損益，不能過也。

translations.literal: Henceforth Tang's texts for the Five Rites were first complete; later ages used them, and though at times there were slight additions and subtractions, they could not surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth Tang's texts for the Five Rites were first complete. later ages used them, and though at times there were slight additions and subtractions, they could not surpass them.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，太常禮院脩撰王涇考次歷代郊廟沿革之制及其工歌祝號，而圖其壇屋陟降之序，為郊祀錄十卷。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era, Wang Jing, compiler of the Court Music Ritual Office, arranged the evolution of suburban and temple systems through the ages and their craft-songs and invocations, diagramming the order of ascending and descending at altars and halls, producing ten scrolls of Suburban Sacrifice Records.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era. Wang Jing, compiler of the Court Music Ritual Office, arranged the evolution of suburban and temple systems through the ages and their craft-songs and invocations, diagramming the order of ascending and descending at altars and halls, producing ten scrolls of Suburban Sacrifice Records.

sentences.zh: 元和十一年，祕書郎、脩撰韋公肅又錄開元已後禮文，損益為禮閣新儀三十卷。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yuanhe, Secretary Gentleman and Compiler Wei Gongsu further recorded ritual texts after Kaiyuan, adding and subtracting to make thirty scrolls of New Ritual Protocol for the Ritual Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yuanhe. Secretary Gentleman and Compiler Wei Gongsu further recorded ritual texts after Kaiyuan, adding and subtracting to make thirty scrolls of New Ritual Protocol for the Ritual Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 十三年，太常博士王彥威為曲臺新禮三十卷，又採元和以來王公士民昏祭喪葬之禮為續曲臺禮三十卷。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Court Music Doctor Wang Yanwei made thirty scrolls of New Ritual for the Qu Terrace, and also gathered from Yuanhe onward the marriage, sacrifice, and burial rites of princes, officials, and commoners into thirty scrolls of Continued Qu Terrace Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year. Court Music Doctor Wang Yanwei made thirty scrolls of New Ritual for the Qu Terrace, and also gathered from Yuanhe onward the marriage, sacrifice, and burial rites of princes, officials, and commoners into thirty scrolls of Continued Qu Terrace Ritual.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，考其文記，可謂備矣，以之施于貞觀、開元之間，亦可謂盛矣，而不能至三代之隆者，具其文而意不在焉，此所謂「禮樂為虛名」也哉！

translations.literal: Alas—examining their written records, one may say they were complete; applied between the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras, one may say they were grand; yet unable to reach the splendor of the Three Dynasties—having the text while the intent was not in it: this is what is called "rites and music as empty names," is it not!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—examining their written records, one may say they were complete. applied between the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras, one may say they were grand. yet unable to reach the splendor of the Three Dynasties—having the text while the intent was not in it: this is what is called "rites and music as empty names," is it not!

sentences.zh: 一曰吉禮。

translations.literal: First, auspicious ritual.
translations.idiomatic: First, auspicious ritual.

sentences.zh: 大祀：天、地、宗廟、五帝及追尊之帝、后。

translations.literal: Great sacrifices: Heaven, Earth, the ancestral temple, the Five Emperors, and emperors and empresses posthumously honored.
translations.idiomatic: Great sacrifices: Heaven. Earth, the ancestral temple, the Five Emperors, and emperors and empresses posthumously honored.

sentences.zh: 中祀：社、稷、日、月、星、辰、岳、鎮、海、瀆、帝社、先蠶、七祀、文宣、武成王及古帝王、贈太子。

translations.literal: Middle sacrifices: the altars of soil and grain, sun, moon, stars, constellations, mountains, garrisons, seas, rivers, the emperor's soil altar, the First Silkworm, the Seven Sacrifices, Kings Wen and Wu, ancient emperors, and posthumously honored crown princes.
translations.idiomatic: Middle sacrifices: the altars of soil and grain, sun, moon, stars, constellations, mountains, garrisons, seas, rivers, the Emperor's soil altar, the First Silkworm, the Seven Sacrifices, Kings Wen and Wu, ancient emperors, and posthumously honored crown princes.

sentences.zh: 小祀：司中、司命、司人、司祿、風伯、雨師、靈星、山林、川澤、司寒、馬祖、先牧、馬社、馬步，州縣之社稷、釋奠。

translations.literal: Minor sacrifices: the Director of Fate, Director of Life, Director of Humanity, Director of Blessings, the Wind Lord, Rain Master, the Spirit Star, mountains, forests, rivers, marshes, the Director of Cold, Horse Ancestor, Former Herds, Horse Soil Altar, Horse Pace—also the soil and grain altars of prefectures and counties, and libation sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Minor sacrifices: the Director of Fate. Director of Life, Director of Humanity, Director of Blessings, the Wind Lord, Rain Master, the Spirit Star, mountains, forests, rivers, marshes, the Director of Cold, Horse Ancestor, Former Herds, Horse Soil Altar, Horse Pace—also the soil and grain altars of prefectures and counties, and libation sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 而天子親祠者二十有四。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven personally sacrifices at twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven personally sacrifices at twenty-four rites.

sentences.zh: 三歲一祫，五歲一禘，當其歲則舉。

translations.literal: Every three years a collective offering, every five years a great offering—when the year comes, they are performed.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years a collective offering. every five years a great offering—when the year comes, they are performed.

sentences.zh: 其餘二十有二，一歲之間不能徧舉，則有司攝事。

translations.literal: Of the remaining twenty-two, within one year they cannot all be performed, so the relevant offices act as deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Of the remaining twenty-two. within one year they cannot all be performed, so the relevant offices act as deputies.

sentences.zh: 其非常祀者，有時而行之。

translations.literal: Irregular sacrifices are performed when the time requires.
translations.idiomatic: Irregular sacrifices are performed when the time requires.

sentences.zh: 而皇后、皇太子歲行事者各一，其餘皆有司行事。

translations.literal: The empress and crown prince each perform one rite per year; the rest are performed by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The empress and crown prince each perform one rite per year. the rest are performed by the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 凡歲之常祀二十有二：冬至、正月上辛，祈穀；

translations.literal: The regular sacrifices of the year number twenty-two: at the winter solstice and on the first xin day of the first month, prayer for grain;
translations.idiomatic: The regular sacrifices of the year number twenty-two: at the winter solstice and on the first xin day of the first month, prayer for grain;.

sentences.zh: 孟夏，雩祀昊天上帝于圓丘；

translations.literal: In the first month of summer, rain sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: At the first month of summer, rain sacrifice to the August Supreme Lord of Heaven at the Round Mound;

sentences.zh: 季秋，大享于明堂；

translations.literal: In the last month of autumn, the great offering in the Bright Hall;
translations.idiomatic: In the last month of autumn, the great offering in the Bright Hall;.

sentences.zh: 臘，蜡百神于南郊；

translations.literal: At the year-end wax offering, wax to the hundred spirits at the southern suburb;
translations.idiomatic: At the year-end wax offering, wax to the hundred spirits at the southern suburb;.

sentences.zh: 春分，朝日于東郊；

translations.literal: At the spring equinox, audience with the sun at the eastern suburb;
translations.idiomatic: At the spring equinox, audience with the sun at the eastern suburb;.

sentences.zh: 秋分，夕月于西郊；

translations.literal: At the autumn equinox, evening audience with the moon at the western suburb;
translations.idiomatic: At the autumn equinox, evening audience with the moon at the western suburb;.

sentences.zh: 夏至，祭地祇于方丘；

translations.literal: At the summer solstice, sacrifice to the Earth Spirit at the Square Mound;
translations.idiomatic: At the summer solstice, sacrifice to the Earth Spirit at the Square Mound;.

sentences.zh: 孟冬，祭神州、地祇于北郊；

translations.literal: In the first month of winter, sacrifice to the Spirit of the Land and Earth Spirit at the northern suburb;
translations.idiomatic: At the first month of winter, sacrifice to the Spirit of the Land and Earth Spirit at the northern suburb;

sentences.zh: 仲春、仲秋上戊，祭于太社；

translations.literal: On the first wu days of the second and eighth months, sacrifice at the Grand Soil Altar;
translations.idiomatic: On the first wu days of the second and eighth months, sacrifice at the Grand Soil Altar;.

sentences.zh: 立春、立夏、季夏之土王、立秋、立冬，祀五帝于四郊；

translations.literal: At the beginning of spring, beginning of summer, the earth's king in the last month of summer, beginning of autumn, and beginning of winter, sacrifice to the Five Emperors at the four suburbs;
translations.idiomatic: In early spring, beginning of summer, the earth's king in the last month of summer, beginning of autumn, and beginning of winter, sacrifice to the Five Emperors at the four suburbs;

sentences.zh: 孟春、孟夏、孟秋、孟冬、臘，享于太廟；

translations.literal: In the first months of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, and at the wax offering, offerings in the Grand Temple;
translations.idiomatic: At the first months of spring, summer, autumn, and winter, and at the wax offering, offerings in the Grand Temple;

sentences.zh: 孟春吉亥，享先農，遂以耕籍。

translations.literal: On the auspicious hai day of the first month of spring, offering to the First Farmer, followed by the plowing ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On the auspicious hai day of the first month of spring. offering to the First Farmer, followed by the plowing ceremony.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀之節有六：一曰卜日，二曰齋戒，三曰陳設，四曰省牲器，五曰奠玉帛、宗廟之晨祼，六曰進熟、饋食。

translations.literal: The stages of sacrifice number six: first, selecting the day; second, purification; third, arranging installations; fourth, inspecting victims and vessels; fifth, presenting jade and silks—or in the ancestral temple, the morning libation; sixth, presenting the cooked offering and presenting food.
translations.idiomatic: The stages of sacrifice number six: first, selecting the day. second, purification. third, arranging installations. fourth, inspecting victims and vessels. fifth, presenting jade and silks—or in the ancestral temple, the morning libation. sixth, presenting the cooked offering and presenting food.

sentences.zh: 一曰卜日。

translations.literal: First, selecting the day.
translations.idiomatic: First, selecting the day.

sentences.zh: 凡大祀、中祀無常日者卜，小祀則筮，皆于太廟。

translations.literal: For great and middle sacrifices without fixed days, tortoise-shell divination is used; for minor sacrifices, yarrow-stalk divination—all at the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: For great and middle sacrifices without fixed days, tortoise-shell divination is used. for minor sacrifices, yarrow-stalk divination—all at the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 卜日，前祀四十有五日，卜于廟南門之外，布卜席闑西閾外。

translations.literal: For selecting the day, forty-five days before the sacrifice, divination is performed outside the southern gate of the temple; the divination mat is spread outside the western threshold of the side gate.
translations.idiomatic: For selecting the day, forty-five days before the sacrifice, divination is performed outside the southern gate of the temple. the divination mat is spread outside the western threshold of the side gate.

sentences.zh: 太常卿立門東，太卜正占者立門西，卜正奠龜於席西首，灼龜之具在龜北，乃執龜立席東，北向。

translations.literal: The Director of Court Music stands east of the gate; the Chief Diviner, who performs the divination, stands west of the gate. The diviner places the tortoise at the west head of the mat; implements for burning the tortoise are north of the tortoise; then holding the tortoise he stands east of the mat, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Court Music stands east of the gate; the Chief Diviner, who performs the divination, stands west of the gate. The diviner places the tortoise at the west head of the mat. implements for burning the tortoise are north of the tortoise. then holding the tortoise he stands east of the mat, facing north.

sentences.zh: 太卜令進受龜，詣卿示高，卿受視已，令受龜，少退俟命。

translations.literal: The Diviner-in-Chief advances to receive the tortoise, goes to the Director to show the height; the Director receives and inspects it; the Diviner-in-Chief receives the tortoise, steps back slightly, and awaits orders.
translations.idiomatic: The Diviner-in-Chief advances to receive the tortoise, goes to the Director to show the height. the Director receives and inspects it. the Diviner-in-Chief receives the tortoise, steps back slightly, and awaits orders.

sentences.zh: 卿曰：「皇帝以某日祗祀於某。

translations.literal: The Director says: "The emperor will on a certain day reverently sacrifice to a certain [deity].
translations.idiomatic: The Director says: "The emperor will on a certain day reverently sacrifice to a certain [deity].

sentences.zh: 」令日：「諾。

translations.literal: " The Diviner-in-Chief says: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: " The Diviner-in-Chief says: "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」遂還席，西向坐。

translations.literal: " Then he returns to the mat and sits facing west.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he returns to the mat and sits facing west.

sentences.zh: 命龜曰：「假爾太龜，有常。

translations.literal: He addresses the tortoise: "I borrow you, great tortoise, according to constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: He addresses the tortoise: "I borrow you. great tortoise, according to constant rule.

sentences.zh: 」興，授卜正龜。

translations.literal: " He rises and hands the tortoise to the Chief Diviner.
translations.idiomatic: " He rises and hands the tortoise to the Chief Diviner.

sentences.zh: 卜正負東扉坐，作龜，興。

translations.literal: The Chief Diviner, bearing the eastern door panel, sits, cracks the tortoise, and rises.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Diviner. bearing the eastern door panel, sits, cracks the tortoise, and rises.

sentences.zh: 令進，受龜，示卿。

translations.literal: The Diviner-in-Chief advances, receives the tortoise, and shows the Director.
translations.idiomatic: The Diviner-in-Chief advances. receives the tortoise, and shows the Director.

sentences.zh: 卿受，反之。

translations.literal: The Director receives it and returns it.
translations.idiomatic: The Director receives it and returns it.

sentences.zh: 令復位，東向，占之，不釋龜，進告於卿曰：「某日從。

translations.literal: The Diviner-in-Chief returns to his place, faces east, divines, without releasing the tortoise, advances and reports to the Director: "A certain day is favorable.
translations.idiomatic: The Diviner-in-Chief returns to his place. faces east, divines, without releasing the tortoise, advances and reports to the Director: "A certain day is favorable.

sentences.zh: 」乃以龜還卜正。

translations.literal: " Then he returns the tortoise to the Chief Diviner.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he returns the tortoise to the Chief Diviner.

sentences.zh: 凡卜日必舉初旬；

translations.literal: Whenever selecting a day, the first ten-day period must be tried;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever selecting a day, the first ten-day period must be tried;.

sentences.zh: 不吉，即繇中及下，如初儀。

translations.literal: if not auspicious, one proceeds through the middle and lower periods as in the first protocol.
translations.idiomatic: If the day is inauspicious, proceed through the middle and lower periods as in the first protocol.

sentences.zh: 若筮日，則卜正啟韇出策，兼執之，受命還席，以韇擊策，述命曰：「假爾太筮，有常。

translations.literal: If divining by yarrow stalks for the day, the Chief Diviner opens the case, takes out the stalks, holds them together, receives orders and returns to the mat, strikes the stalks with the case, and states the charge: "I borrow you, great yarrow, according to constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: If divining by yarrow stalks for the day; the Chief Diviner opens the case, takes out the stalks, holds them together, receives orders and returns to the mat, strikes the stalks with the case, and states the charge: "I borrow you, great yarrow, according to constant rule.

sentences.zh: 」乃釋韇坐策，執卦以示，如卜儀。

translations.literal: " Then he sets down the case, sits on the stalks, holds up the hexagram to show—as in the tortoise protocol.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he sets down the case. sits on the stalks, holds up the hexagram to show—as in the tortoise protocol.

sentences.zh: 小祀筮日，則太卜令莅之，日吉乃用，遇廢務皆勿避。

translations.literal: For minor sacrifices' stalk divination, the Diviner-in-Chief presides; when the day is auspicious it is used; even if it falls on a day when regular duties are suspended, none are avoided.
translations.idiomatic: For minor sacrifices' stalk divination, the Diviner-in-Chief presides. when the day is auspicious it is used. even if it falls on a day when regular duties are suspended, none are avoided.

sentences.zh: 二曰齋戒。

translations.literal: Second, purification.
translations.idiomatic: Second, purification.

sentences.zh: 其別有三：曰散齋，曰致齋，曰清齋。

translations.literal: The distinctions are three: called scattered purification, called concentrated purification, called pure purification.
translations.idiomatic: The distinctions are three: scattered purification, concentrated purification, and pure purification.

sentences.zh: 大祀，散齋四日，致齋三日；

translations.literal: For great sacrifices, scattered purification four days, concentrated purification three days;
translations.idiomatic: For great sacrifices. scattered purification four days, concentrated purification three days;

sentences.zh: 中祀，散齋三日，致齋二日；

translations.literal: for middle sacrifices, scattered purification three days, concentrated purification two days;
translations.idiomatic: for middle sacrifices. scattered purification three days, concentrated purification two days;

sentences.zh: 小祀，散齋二日，致齋一日。

translations.literal: for minor sacrifices, scattered purification two days, concentrated purification one day.
translations.idiomatic: for minor sacrifices. scattered purification two days, concentrated purification one day.

sentences.zh: 大祀，前期七日，太尉誓百官於尚書省曰：「某日祀某神祇于某所，各揚其職。

translations.literal: For great sacrifices, seven days before, the Grand Marshal swears in the hundred officials at the Ministry of Personnel, saying: "On a certain day we sacrifice to a certain spirit at a certain place; each display your duty. Those who do not supply their tasks— the state has its constant punishments.
translations.idiomatic: For great sacrifices, seven days before, the Grand Marshal swears in the hundred officials at the Ministry of Personnel, saying: "On a certain day we sacrifice to a certain spirit at a certain place; each display your duty. Those who do not supply their tasks—the state has its constant punishments.

sentences.zh: 不供其事，國有常刑。

translations.literal: " Then purification begins.
translations.idiomatic: " Then purification begins.

sentences.zh: 」於是乃齋。

translations.literal: " The emperor's scattered purification is in a separate hall;
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's scattered purification is in a separate hall;

sentences.zh: 皇帝散齋于別殿；

translations.literal: for concentrated purification, two days in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, one day at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: for concentrated purification. two days in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, one day at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 致齋，其二日于太極殿，一日于行宮。

translations.literal: One day before concentrated purification, the Imperial Household Attendant sets the imperial canopy in the western wing of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and in the inner chambers—all facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One day before concentrated purification, the Imperial Household Attendant sets the imperial canopy in the western wing of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and in the inner chambers—facing east.

sentences.zh: 前致齋一日，尚舍奉御設御幄於太極殿西序及室內，皆東向。

translations.literal: One day before concentrated purification, the Imperial Household Attendant sets the imperial canopy in the western wing of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and in the inner chambers—all facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One day before concentrated purification, the Imperial Household Attendant sets the imperial canopy in the western wing of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate and in the inner chambers—facing east.

sentences.zh: 尚舍直長張帷於前楹下。

translations.literal: The Chief of the Imperial Household stretches curtains beneath the front pillars.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief of the Imperial Household stretches curtains beneath the front pillars.

sentences.zh: 致齋之日，質明，諸衞勒所部屯門列仗。

translations.literal: On the day of concentrated purification, at dawn, the guards of the various commands array troops at the gates.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of concentrated purification. at dawn, the guards of the various commands array troops at the gates.

sentences.zh: 晝漏上水一刻，侍中版奏「請中嚴」。

translations.literal: At the first quarter after the day clepsydra begins, the attendant-in-chief reports by tablet: "Request mid-strictness."
translations.idiomatic: At the first quarter after the day clepsydra begins, the attendant-in-chief reports by tablet: "Request mid-strictness.".

sentences.zh: 諸衞之屬各督其隊入陳於殿庭，通事舍人引文武五品已上袴褶陪位，諸侍衞之官服其器服，諸侍臣齋者結佩，詣閤奉迎。

translations.literal: Subordinates of the various guards each lead their companies into formation in the palace courtyard; remonstrance clerks lead civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above in military dress to attendance positions; attendant guards wear their equipment; attending ministers in purification fasten their sashes and go to the gate to welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates of the various guards lead their companies into formation in the palace courtyard. remonstrance clerks lead civil and military officials of the fifth rank and above in military dress to attendance positions. attendant guards wear their equipment. attending ministers in purification fasten their sashes and go to the gate to welcome.

sentences.zh: 二刻，侍中版奏「外辦」。

translations.literal: At the second quarter, the attendant-in-chief reports by tablet: "Outer preparations complete."
translations.idiomatic: At the second quarter, the attendant-in-chief reports by tablet: "Outer preparations complete.".

sentences.zh: 三刻，皇帝服衮冕，結佩，乘輿出自西房，曲直華蓋，警蹕侍衞，即御座，東向，侍臣夾侍。

translations.literal: At the third quarter, the emperor dons the dragon robe and coronet, fastens his sash, rides the palanquin out from the western chamber, with curved canopy and imperial escort, and takes the throne facing east, with attending ministers on either side.
translations.idiomatic: At the third quarter, the Emperor dons the dragon robe and coronet, fastens his sash, rides the palanquin out from the western chamber, with curved canopy and imperial escort, and takes the throne facing east, with attending ministers on either side.

sentences.zh: 一刻頃，侍中前跪奏稱：「侍中臣某言，請就齋室。

translations.literal: After about one quarter, the attendant-in-chief kneels forward and reports: "The attendant-in-chief, your servant, requests that Your Majesty proceed to the purification chamber."
translations.idiomatic: After about one quarter; the attendant-in-chief kneels forward and reports: "The attendant-in-chief, your servant, requests that Your Majesty proceed to the purification chamber."

sentences.zh: 」皇帝降座入室，文武侍臣還本司，陪位者以次出。

translations.literal: " The emperor descends from the throne and enters the chamber; civil and military attendants return to their offices; those in attendance positions leave in order.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor descends from the throne and enters the chamber. civil and military attendants return to their offices. those in attendance positions leave in order.

sentences.zh: 凡豫祀之官，散齋理事如舊，唯不弔喪問疾，不作樂，不判署刑殺文書，不行刑罰，不預穢惡。

translations.literal: For all officials participating in the sacrifice, during scattered purification they handle affairs as usual, only not condoling the bereaved or inquiring after the ill, not making music, not signing documents on punishments and executions, not carrying out punishments, not attending what is defiling.
translations.idiomatic: For all officials participating in the sacrifice. during scattered purification they handle affairs as usual, only not condoling the bereaved or inquiring after the ill, not making music, not signing documents on punishments and executions, not carrying out punishments, not attending what is defiling.

sentences.zh: 致齋，唯行祀事，其祀官已齋而闕者攝。

translations.literal: During concentrated purification, only sacrificial affairs are performed; if a sacrificial officer is in purification but absent, another acts as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: During concentrated purification, only sacrificial affairs are performed. if a sacrificial officer is in purification but absent, another acts as deputy.

sentences.zh: 其餘清齋一日。

translations.literal: The rest observe pure purification for one day.
translations.idiomatic: The rest observe pure purification for one day.

sentences.zh: 三曰陳設。

translations.literal: Third, arranging installations.
translations.idiomatic: Third, arranging installations.

sentences.zh: 其別有五：有待事之次，有即事之位，有門外之位，有牲器之位，有席神之位。

translations.literal: The distinctions are five: places for awaiting affairs, positions for immediate affairs, positions outside the gate, positions for victims and vessels, positions for seating the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The distinctions are five: places for awaiting affairs. positions for immediate affairs, positions outside the gate, positions for victims and vessels, positions for seating the spirits.

sentences.zh: 前祀三日，尚舍直長施大次於外壝東門之內道北，南向。

translations.literal: Three days before the sacrifice, the Chief of the Imperial Household erects the great canopy inside the eastern gate of the outer enclosure on the north side of the road, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Three days before the sacrifice; the Chief of the Imperial Household erects the great canopy inside the eastern gate of the outer enclosure on the north side of the road, facing south.

sentences.zh: 衞尉設文武侍臣之次於其前，左右相向。

translations.literal: The Commandant of the Guard sets the canopy for civil and military attendant ministers before it, left and right facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of the Guard arrays canopies for civil and military attendant ministers before it, left and right facing each other.

sentences.zh: 設祀官次於東壝之外道南，從祀文官九品於其東，東方、南方朝集使又於其東，蕃客又於其東，重行異位，北向西上。

translations.literal: Sacrificial officers' canopies are set south of the road outside the eastern enclosure; civil officials of the ninth rank who accompany the sacrifice are east of them; envoys from the eastern and southern regions further east; foreign guests further east—double rows in separate positions, north-facing, west ascending.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial officers' canopies stand south of the road outside the eastern enclosure. civil officials of the ninth rank who accompany the sacrifice are east of them. envoys from the eastern and southern regions further east. foreign guests further east—double rows in separate positions, north-facing, west ascending.

sentences.zh: 介公、酅公於西壝之外道南，武官九品於其西，西方、北方朝集使又於其西，蕃客又於其西，東上。

translations.literal: The Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi south of the road outside the western enclosure; military officials of the ninth rank west of them; envoys from the western and northern regions further west; foreign guests further west—east ascending.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi south of the road outside the western enclosure. military officials of the ninth rank west of them. envoys from the western and northern regions further west. foreign guests further west—east ascending.

sentences.zh: 其褒聖侯若在朝，位於文官三品下。

translations.literal: If the Marquis Who Honors the Sage is at court, his position is below civil officials of the third rank.
translations.idiomatic: If the Marquis Who Honors the Sage is at court, his position is below civil officials of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 設陳饌幔於內壝東西門之外道北，南向；

translations.literal: Food-offering curtains are set north of the road outside the inner enclosure's east and west gates, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: Food-offering curtains stand north of the road outside the inner enclosure's east and west gates, facing south;

sentences.zh: 北門之外道東，西向。

translations.literal: east of the road outside the north gate, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: east of the road outside the north gate, facing west.

sentences.zh: 明日，奉禮郎設御位於壇之東南，西向；

translations.literal: The next day, the Master of Ceremonies sets the imperial position southeast of the altar, facing west;
translations.idiomatic: The next day, the Master of Ceremonies set the imperial position southeast of the altar, facing west;

sentences.zh: 望燎位當柴壇之北，南向；

translations.literal: the position for gazing at the fire-offering north of the firewood altar, facing south;
translations.idiomatic: The position for gazing at the fire-offering lay north of the firewood altar, facing south;

sentences.zh: 祀官公卿位於內壝東門之內道南，分獻之官於公卿之南，執事者又於其後，異位重行，西向北上。

translations.literal: One southwest, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One southwest, facing east.

sentences.zh: 御史位於壇下，一在東南，西向；

translations.literal: One southwest, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One southwest, facing east.

sentences.zh: 一在西南，東向。

translations.literal: One southwest, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One southwest, facing east.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎位於樂縣東北，贊者在南，差退，皆西向。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies northeast of the music stand; presenters south, slightly back—all facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies northeast of the music stand. presenters south, slightly back—facing west.

sentences.zh: 又設奉禮郎、贊者位於燎壇東北，西向。

translations.literal: Again the Master of Ceremonies and presenters are set northeast of the fire altar, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Again the Master of Ceremonies and presenters stand northeast of the fire altar, facing west.

sentences.zh: 皆北上。

translations.literal: All north ascending.
translations.idiomatic: All north ascending.

sentences.zh: 協律郎位於壇上南陛之西，東向。

translations.literal: The Pitch-Pipe Master west of the southern steps on the altar, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The Pitch-Pipe Master west of the southern steps on the altar, facing east.

sentences.zh: 太樂令位於北縣之間，當壇北向。

translations.literal: The Director of Court Music between the northern stands, facing the altar north.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Court Music between the northern stands, facing the altar north.

sentences.zh: 從祀文官九品位於執事之南，東方、南方朝集使又於其南，蕃客又於其南，西向北上。

translations.literal: Civil officials of the ninth rank who accompany the sacrifice south of the attendants; envoys from the eastern and southern regions further south; foreign guests further south—west-facing, north ascending.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of the ninth rank who accompany the sacrifice south of the attendants. envoys from the eastern and southern regions further south. foreign guests further south—west-facing, north ascending.

sentences.zh: 介公、酅公位於中壝西門之內道南，武官九品又於其南，西方、北方朝集使又於其南，蕃客又於其南，東向北上。

translations.literal: These are for immediate performance.
translations.idiomatic: These positions are where officers perform the rite on the spot.

sentences.zh: 所以即而行事也。

translations.literal: These are for immediate performance.
translations.idiomatic: These positions are where officers perform the rite on the spot.

sentences.zh: 又設祀官及從祀羣官位於東西壝門之外，如設次，所以省牲及祀之日將入而序立也。

translations.literal: Again sacrificial officers and accompanying officials are set outside the east and west gates of the enclosure, as when setting canopies—so that when inspecting victims and on the sacrifice day they enter and stand in order.
translations.idiomatic: Again sacrificial officers and accompanying officials stand outside the east and west gates of the enclosure, as when setting canopies—so that when inspecting victims and on the sacrifice day they enter and stand in order.

sentences.zh: 設牲牓於東壝之外，當門西向。

translations.literal: The victim placard is set outside the eastern enclosure, west of the gate, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The victim placard stands outside the eastern enclosure, west of the gate, facing west.

sentences.zh: 蒼牲一居前，又蒼牲一、又青牲一在北，少退南上。

translations.literal: One azure victim in front; again one azure victim and one green victim to the north, slightly back, south ascending.
translations.idiomatic: One azure victim in front. again one azure victim and one green victim to the north, slightly back, south ascending.

sentences.zh: 次赤牲一、次黃牲一、白牲一、玄牲一、又赤牲一、白牲一在南，少退北上。

translations.literal: Next one red victim, one yellow victim, one white victim, one black victim, again one red victim and one white victim to the south, slightly back, north ascending.
translations.idiomatic: Next one red victim. one yellow victim, one white victim, one black victim, again one red victim and one white victim to the south, slightly back, north ascending.

sentences.zh: 廩犧令位於牲西南，祝史陪其後，皆北向。

translations.literal: The Director of Imperial Victims southwest of the victims; invokers behind him—all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Imperial Victims southwest of the victims. invokers behind him—facing north.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝位於牲東，各當牲後，祝史陪其後，西向。

translations.literal: The various Chief Invokers east of the victims, each behind his victim; invokers behind them, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: All Chief Invokers east of the victims, each behind his victim. invokers behind them, facing west.

sentences.zh: 太常卿位於牲前少北，御史位於其西，皆南向。

translations.literal: The Director of Court Music slightly north before the victims; censors west of him—all facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Court Music slightly north before the victims. censors west of him—facing south.

sentences.zh: 又設酒尊之位。

translations.literal: Again wine-vessel positions are set.
translations.idiomatic: Again wine-vessel positions stand.

sentences.zh: 上帝，太尊、著尊、犧尊、山罍各二，在壇上東南隅，北向；

translations.literal: For the August Lord, two Grand Vessels, two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, and two Mountain Urns on the southeast corner of the altar, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: For the August Lord. two Grand Vessels, two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, and two Mountain Urns on the southeast corner of the altar, facing north;

sentences.zh: 象尊、壺尊、山罍各二，在壇下南陛之東，北向，俱西上。

translations.literal: two Elephant Vessels, two Pot Vessels, and two Mountain Urns east of the southern steps below the altar, facing north—all west ascending.
translations.idiomatic: two Elephant Vessels. two Pot Vessels, and two Mountain Urns east of the southern steps below the altar, facing north—all west ascending.

sentences.zh: 配帝，著尊、犧尊、象尊、山罍各二，在壇上，於上帝酒尊之東，北向西上。

translations.literal: For the accompanying emperor, two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Elephant Vessels, and two Mountain Urns on the altar east of the August Lord's wine vessels—north-facing, west ascending.
translations.idiomatic: For the accompanying emperor. two Display Vessels, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Elephant Vessels, and two Mountain Urns on the altar east of the August Lord's wine vessels—north-facing, west ascending.

sentences.zh: 五帝、日、月各太尊二，在第一等。

translations.literal: For the Five Emperors, sun, and moon, each two Grand Vessels in the first tier.
translations.idiomatic: For the Five Emperors, sun, and moon, each two Grand Vessels At the first tier.

sentences.zh: 內官每陛間各象尊二，在第二等。

translations.literal: For inner officials, two Elephant Vessels between each flight of steps in the second tier.
translations.idiomatic: For inner officials, two Elephant Vessels between every flight of steps in the second tier.

sentences.zh: 中官每陛間各壺尊二，在第三等。

translations.literal: For middle officials, two Pot Vessels between each flight of steps in the third tier.
translations.idiomatic: For middle officials, two Pot Vessels between every flight of steps in the third tier.

sentences.zh: 外官每道間各概尊二，於下壇下。

translations.literal: For outer officials, two Pouring Vessels between each path below the lower altar.
translations.idiomatic: For outer officials, two Pouring Vessels between every path below the lower altar.

sentences.zh: 眾星每道間各散尊二，於內壝之外。

translations.literal: For the multitude of stars, two Scattered Vessels between each path outside the inner enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: For the multitude of stars, two Scattered Vessels between every path outside the inner enclosure.

sentences.zh: 凡尊，設於神座之左而右向。

translations.literal: For all vessels, they are set to the left of the spirit seat and face right.
translations.idiomatic: For all vessels, they stand to the left of the spirit seat and face right.

sentences.zh: 尊皆加勺冪，五帝、日、月以上，皆有坫，以置爵也。

translations.literal: All vessels have ladles and covers added; for the Five Emperors, sun, moon, and above, all have stands for placing cups.
translations.idiomatic: All vessels have ladles and covers added. for the Five Emperors, sun, moon, and above, all have stands for placing cups.

sentences.zh: 設御洗於午陛東南，亞獻、終獻同洗於卯陛之南，皆北向。

translations.literal: The imperial washing place southeast of the wu steps; secondary and final offerings share a wash south of the mao steps—all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial washing place southeast of the wu steps. secondary and final offerings share a wash south of the mao steps—facing north.

sentences.zh: 罍水在洗東，篚在洗西，南肆。

translations.literal: Water urns east of the wash; baskets west of the wash, displayed to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Water urns east of the wash. baskets west of the wash, displayed to the south.

sentences.zh: 篚，實以巾爵也。

translations.literal: The baskets hold cloth-wrapped cups.
translations.idiomatic: The baskets hold cloth-wrapped cups.

sentences.zh: 分獻，罍、洗、篚、冪各於其方陛道之左，內向。

translations.literal: For separate offerings, urns, wash, baskets, and covers each on the left of their side's steps and path, facing inward.
translations.idiomatic: For separate offerings. urns, wash, baskets, and covers each on the left of their side's steps and path, facing inward.

sentences.zh: 執尊、罍、篚、冪者，各立於其後。

translations.literal: Those holding vessels, urns, baskets, and covers each stand behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Those holding vessels. urns, baskets, and covers each stand behind them.

sentences.zh: 玉幣之篚於壇上下尊坫之所。

translations.literal: Baskets for jade and silks at the stands of vessels on and below the altar.
translations.idiomatic: Baskets for jade and silks at the stands of vessels on and below the altar.

sentences.zh: 前祀一日，晡後，太史令、郊社令各常服，帥其屬升，設昊天上帝神座於壇上北方，南向，席以槀秸。

translations.literal: One day before the sacrifice, after the afternoon, the Astronomical Director and Suburban Altar Director each in regular dress lead their subordinates up and set the spirit seat of the August Supreme Lord of Heaven on the altar in the north, facing south, with straw mat seating.
translations.idiomatic: One day before the sacrifice, after the afternoon, the Astronomical Director and Suburban Altar Director each in regular dress lead their subordinates up and set the spirit seat of the August Supreme Lord of Heaven on the altar in the north, facing south, with straw mat seating.

sentences.zh: 高祖神堯皇帝神座於東方，西向，席以莞。

translations.literal: The spirit seat of the High Ancestor Emperor Shenyao in the east, facing west, with rush mat seating.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit seat of the High Ancestor Emperor Shenyao in the east, facing west, with rush mat seating.

sentences.zh: 五方帝、日、月於壇第一等，青帝於東陛之北，赤帝於南陛之東，黃帝於南陛之西，白帝於西陛之南，黑帝於北陛之西，大明於東陛之南，夜明於西陛之北，席皆以槀秸。

translations.literal: The Five Directional Emperors, sun, and moon on the altar's first tier—the Green Emperor north of the eastern steps, Red Emperor east of the southern steps, Yellow Emperor west of the southern steps, White Emperor south of the western steps, Black Emperor west of the northern steps, Great Brightness south of the eastern steps, Night Brightness north of the western steps—all with straw mat seating.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Directional Emperors. sun, and moon on the altar's first tier—the Green Emperor north of the eastern steps, Red Emperor east of the southern steps, Yellow Emperor west of the southern steps, White Emperor south of the western steps, Black Emperor west of the northern steps, Great Brightness south of the eastern steps, Night Brightness north of the western steps—all with straw mat seating.

sentences.zh: 五星、十二辰、河漢及內官五十有五於第二等十有二陛之間，各依其方，席皆內向。

translations.literal: The Five Stars, twelve chronograms, the River Han, and fifty-five inner officials on the second tier among the twelve flights of steps, each according to its direction, seats all facing inward.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Stars, twelve chronograms, the River Han, and fifty-five inner officials on the second tier among the twelve flights of steps, each according to its direction, seats facing inward.

sentences.zh: 其內官有北辰座於東陛之北，曜魄寶於北陛之西，北斗於南陛之東，天一、太一皆在北斗之東，五帝內座於曜魄寶之東，皆差在前。

translations.literal: Among inner officials there is the North Star seat north of the eastern steps, Shining Soul Treasure west of the northern steps, Northern Dipper east of the southern steps, Celestial One and Supreme One both east of the Northern Dipper, the Five Emperors' inner seats east of Shining Soul Treasure—all slightly forward.
translations.idiomatic: Among inner officials there is the North Star seat north of the eastern steps. Shining Soul Treasure west of the northern steps, Northern Dipper east of the southern steps, Celestial One and Supreme One both east of the Northern Dipper, the Five Emperors' inner seats east of Shining Soul Treasure—all slightly forward.

sentences.zh: 二十八宿及中官一百五十有九於第三等，其二十八宿及帝座、七公、日星、帝席、大角、攝提、太微、太子、明堂、軒轅、三台、五車、諸王、月星、織女、建星、天紀等一十有七皆差在前。

translations.literal: The twenty-eight lunar mansions and one hundred fifty-nine middle officials on the third tier; of the twenty-eight mansions and Imperial Seat, Seven Elders, Sun Star, Emperor's Seat, Great Horn, Triumphant Arch, Supreme Palace, Heir Apparent, Bright Hall, Chariot Axis, Three Terraces, Five Chariots, Various Kings, Moon Star, Weaver Girl, Establishment Star, Celestial Record, and seventeen others—all slightly forward.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-eight lunar mansions and one hundred fifty-nine middle officials on the third tier. of the twenty-eight mansions and Imperial Seat, Seven Elders, Sun Star, Emperor's Seat, Great Horn, Triumphant Arch, Supreme Palace, Heir Apparent, Bright Hall, Chariot Axis, Three Terraces, Five Chariots, Various Kings, Moon Star, Weaver Girl, Establishment Star, Celestial Record, and seventeen others—all slightly forward.

sentences.zh: 外官一百有五於內壝之內，眾星三百六十於內壝之外，各依方次十有二道之間，席皆以莞。

translations.literal: One hundred five outer officials inside the inner enclosure; three hundred sixty multitude stars outside the inner enclosure, each according to directional order among the twelve paths—seating all rush mats.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred five outer officials inside the inner enclosure. three hundred sixty multitude stars outside the inner enclosure, each according to directional order among the twelve paths—seating all rush mats.

sentences.zh: 若在宗廟，則前享三日，尚舍直長施大次於廟東門之外道北，南向。

translations.literal: If at the ancestral temple, then three days before the offering, the Chief of the Imperial Household erects the great canopy north of the road outside the temple's east gate, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: If at the ancestral temple. then three days before the offering, the Chief of the Imperial Household erects the great canopy north of the road outside the temple's east gate, facing south.

sentences.zh: 守宮設文武侍臣次於其後，文左武右，俱南向。

translations.literal: The Palace Keeper sets civil and military attendant ministers' canopies behind it—civil left, military right, all facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Keeper sets civil and military attendant ministers' canopies behind it—civil left, military right, facing south.

sentences.zh: 設諸享官、九廟子孫於齋坊內道東近南，西向北上。

translations.literal: All offering officers and descendants of the nine temples east inside the purification quarters near the south—west-facing, north ascending.
translations.idiomatic: All offering officers and descendants of the nine temples east inside the purification quarters near the south—west-facing, north ascending.

sentences.zh: 文官九品又於其南，東方、南方蕃客又於其南，西向北上。

translations.literal: Civil officials of the ninth rank further south; eastern and southern foreign guests further south—west-facing, north ascending.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of the ninth rank further south. eastern and southern foreign guests further south—west-facing, north ascending.

sentences.zh: 介公、酅公於廟西門之外，近南。

translations.literal: The Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi outside the temple's west gate, near the south.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi outside the temple's west gate, near the south.

sentences.zh: 武官九品於其南，西方、北方蕃客又於其南，東向北上。

translations.literal: Military officials of the ninth rank south of them; western and northern foreign guests further south—east-facing, north ascending.
translations.idiomatic: Military officials of the ninth rank south of them. western and northern foreign guests further south—east-facing, north ascending.

sentences.zh: 前享一日，奉禮郎設御位於廟東南，西向。

translations.literal: One day before the offering, the Master of Ceremonies sets the imperial position southeast of the temple, facing west.
translations.idiomatic: One day before the offering; the Master of Ceremonies sets the imperial position southeast of the temple, facing west.

sentences.zh: 設享官公卿位於東門之內道南，執事者位於其後，西向北上。

translations.literal: One southwest, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One southwest, facing east.

sentences.zh: 御史位於廟堂之下，一在東南，西向；

translations.literal: One southwest, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One southwest, facing east.

sentences.zh: 一在西南，東向。

translations.literal: One southwest, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: One southwest, facing east.

sentences.zh: 令史各陪其後。

translations.literal: Clerks each attend behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks every attend behind them.

sentences.zh: 奉禮郎位於樂縣東北，贊者二人，在南差退，俱西向。

translations.literal: The Master of Ceremonies northeast of the music stand; two presenters south, slightly back—all facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The Master of Ceremonies northeast of the music stand. two presenters south, slightly back—facing west.

sentences.zh: 協律郎位於廟堂上前楹之間，近西，東向。

translations.literal: The Pitch-Pipe Master between the front pillars of the temple hall, near the west, facing east.
translations.idiomatic: The Pitch-Pipe Master between the front pillars of the temple hall. near the west, facing east.

sentences.zh: 太樂令位於北縣之間，北向。

translations.literal: The Director of Court Music between the northern stands, facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of Court Music between the northern stands, facing north.

sentences.zh: 設從享之官位，九廟子孫於享官公卿之南，昭、穆異位。

translations.literal: Positions for accompanying officers: descendants of the nine temples south of offering officers and grandees, zhao and mu in separate positions.
translations.idiomatic: Positions for accompanying officers: descendants of the nine temples south of offering officers and grandees, zhao and mu in separate positions.

sentences.zh: 文官九品以上，又於其南，東方、南方蕃客又於其南，西向北上。

translations.literal: Civil officials of the ninth rank and above further south; eastern and southern foreign guests further south—west-facing, north ascending.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of the ninth rank and above further south. eastern and southern foreign guests further south—west-facing, north ascending.

sentences.zh: 介公、酅公位於西門之內道南，武官九品於其南，少西，西方、北方蕃客又於其南，東向北上。

translations.literal: The Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi south of the road inside the west gate; military officials of the ninth rank south of them, slightly west; western and northern foreign guests further south—east-facing, north ascending.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Jie and Duke of Xi south of the road inside the west gate. military officials of the ninth rank south of them, slightly west. western and northern foreign guests further south—east-facing, north ascending.

sentences.zh: 設牲牓於東門之外，如郊之位。

translations.literal: The victim placard outside the east gate, as at the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: The victim placard outside the east gate, as at the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 設尊彝之位於廟堂之上下，每座斝彝一，黃彝一，犧尊、象尊、著尊、山罍各二，在堂上，皆於神座之左。

translations.literal: Vessel positions above and below the temple hall: for each seat one Jia vessel, one Yellow vessel, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Elephant Vessels, two Display Vessels, two Mountain Urns on the hall—all to the left of the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: Vessel positions above and below the temple hall: for each seat one Jia vessel. one Yellow vessel, two Sacrificial Vessels, two Elephant Vessels, two Display Vessels, two Mountain Urns on the hall—all to the left of the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 獻祖、太祖、高祖、高宗尊彝在前楹間，北向；

translations.literal: The honored vessels of the Founding Ancestor, Great Ancestor, High Ancestor, and Gaozong were in the front bays between pillars, facing north;
translations.idiomatic: The ritual vessels of Xianzu, Taizu, Gaozu, and Gaozong stood in the front intercolumnar space, facing north;

sentences.zh: 懿祖、代祖、太宗、中宗、睿宗尊彝在戶外，南向。

translations.literal: The honored vessels of Yizu, Daizu, Taizong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong were outside the doors, facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual vessels of Yizu, Daizu, Taizong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong stood outside the hall doors, facing south.

sentences.zh: 各有坫焉。

translations.literal: Each has a stand.
translations.idiomatic: Each has a stand.

sentences.zh: 其壺尊二、太尊二、山罍四，皆在堂下階間，北向西上；

translations.literal: Two Pot Vessels, two Grand Vessels, four Mountain Urns all between the steps below the hall, north-facing, west ascending;
translations.idiomatic: Two Pot Vessels. two Grand Vessels, four Mountain Urns all between the steps below the hall, north-facing, west ascending;

sentences.zh: 簋、鈃、籩、豆在堂上，俱東側階之北。

translations.literal: gui, xing, bian, and dou vessels on the hall, all north of the eastern side steps.
translations.idiomatic: gui. xing, bian, and dou vessels on the hall, all north of the eastern side steps.

sentences.zh: 每座四簋居前，四簠次之，六豋次之，六鈃次之，籩、豆為後，皆以南為上，屈陳而下。

translations.literal: For each seat four gui in front, four fu next, six deng next, six xing next, bian and dou last—all with south as upper, bending down in rows.
translations.idiomatic: For each seat four gui in front. four fu next, six deng next, six xing next, bian and dou last—all with south as upper, bending down in rows.

sentences.zh: 御洗在東階東南，亞獻又於東南，俱北向。

translations.literal: The imperial wash southeast of the eastern steps; secondary offering again southeast—all facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial wash southeast of the eastern steps. secondary offering again southeast—facing north.

sentences.zh: 罍水在洗東，篚在洗西，南肆。

translations.literal: Water urns east of the wash; baskets west of the wash, displayed to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Water urns east of the wash. baskets west of the wash, displayed to the south.

sentences.zh: 享日，未明五刻，太廟令服其服，布昭、穆之座於戶外，自西序以東：獻祖、太祖、高祖、高宗皆北廂南向，懿祖、代祖、太宗、中宗、睿宗南廂北向。

translations.literal: On the offering day, at the fifth quarter before dawn, the Temple Director dons his robes and arranges zhao and mu seats outside the doors, from the western wing eastward: Offering Ancestor, Great Ancestor, High Ancestor, and High Zong all in the north wing facing south; Esteemed Ancestor, Substitute Ancestor, Taizong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong in the south wing facing north.
translations.idiomatic: On the offering day, at the fifth quarter before dawn, the Temple Director dons his robes and arranges zhao and mu seats outside the doors, from the western wing eastward: Offering Ancestor, Great Ancestor, High Ancestor, and High Zong all in the north wing facing south. Esteemed Ancestor, Substitute Ancestor, Taizong, Zhongzong, and Ruizong in the south wing facing north.

sentences.zh: 每座黼扆，莞席紛純，藻席畫純，次席黼純，左右几。

translations.literal: For each seat black-lacquered screen, rush mat with red border, painted rush mat with patterned border, secondary mat with patterned border, left and right tables.
translations.idiomatic: For each seat black-lacquered screen. rush mat with red border, painted rush mat with patterned border, secondary mat with patterned border, left and right tables.

sentences.zh: 四曰省牲器。

translations.literal: Fourth, inspecting victims and vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, inspecting victims and vessels.

sentences.zh: 省牲之日，午後十刻，去壇二百步所，禁行人。

translations.literal: On the day of inspecting victims, at the tenth quarter after noon, two hundred paces from the altar, travelers are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of inspecting victims. at the tenth quarter after noon, two hundred paces from the altar, travelers are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 晡後二刻，郊社令、丞帥府史三人及齋郎，以尊、坫、罍、洗、篚、冪入設於位。

translations.literal: At the second quarter after the afternoon, the Suburban Altar Director and Assistant lead three clerks of the office and purification youths to bring vessels, stands, urns, wash, baskets, and covers in and set them at their positions.
translations.idiomatic: At the second quarter after the afternoon; the Suburban Altar Director and Assistant lead three clerks of the office and purification youths to bring vessels, stands, urns, wash, baskets, and covers in and set them at their positions.

sentences.zh: 三刻，謁者、贊引各引祀官、公卿及牲皆就位。

translations.literal: At the third quarter, ushers and presenters each lead sacrificial officers, grandees, and victims into position.
translations.idiomatic: At the third quarter, ushers and presenters lead sacrificial officers, grandees, and victims into position.

sentences.zh: 謁者引司空，贊引引御史，入詣壇東陛，升，行掃除於上，降，行樂縣於下。

translations.literal: The usher leads the Minister of Works; the presenter leads the censor—they enter to the eastern steps of the altar, ascend, sweep above, descend, and sweep below at the music stands.
translations.idiomatic: The usher leads the Minister of Works. the presenter leads the censor—they enter to the eastern steps of the altar, ascend, sweep above, descend, and sweep below at the music stands.

sentences.zh: 初，司空將升，謁者引太常卿，贊引引御史，入詣壇東陛，升，視滌濯，降，就省牲位，南向立。

translations.literal: At first, when the Minister of Works is about to ascend, the usher leads the Director of Court Music and the presenter leads the censor—they enter to the eastern steps, ascend, inspect washing, descend, and take position at the victim inspection place, standing facing south.
translations.idiomatic: At first. when the Minister of Works is about to ascend, the usher leads the Director of Court Music and the presenter leads the censor—they enter to the eastern steps, ascend, inspect washing, descend, and take position at the victim inspection place, standing facing south.

sentences.zh: 廩犧令少前，曰：「請省牲。

translations.literal: " The Director of Imperial Victims steps forward slightly and says: "Please inspect the victims."
translations.idiomatic: " The Director of Imperial Victims steps forward slightly and says: "Please inspect the victims.".

sentences.zh: 」太常卿省牲。

translations.literal: " The Director of Court Music inspects the victims.
translations.idiomatic: " The Director of Court Music inspects the victims.

sentences.zh: 廩犧令北面舉手曰：「腯。

translations.literal: " The Director of Imperial Victims, facing north, raises his hand and says: "Fat."
translations.idiomatic: " The Director of Imperial Victims, facing north, raises his hand and says: "Fat."

sentences.zh: 」諸太祝各循牲一匝。

translations.literal: " The various Chief Invokers each circle a victim once.
translations.idiomatic: " All Chief Invokers each circle a victim once.

sentences.zh: 西向舉手曰：「充。

translations.literal: " Facing west, they raise their hands and say: "Full."
translations.idiomatic: " Facing west, they raise their hands and say: "Full."

sentences.zh: 」諸太祝與廩犧令以次牽牲詣廚，授太官。

translations.literal: " The Chief Invokers and Director of Imperial Victims in order lead the victims to the kitchen and hand them to the Imperial Kitchen Director.
translations.idiomatic: " The Chief Invokers and Director of Imperial Victims in order lead the victims to the kitchen and hand them to the Imperial Kitchen Director.

sentences.zh: 謁者引光祿卿詣廚，省鼎鑊，申視濯溉。

translations.literal: The usher leads the Director of the Imperial Commissariat to the kitchen to inspect the cauldrons and report on washing.
translations.idiomatic: " The usher leads the Director of the Imperial Commissariat to the kitchen to inspect the cauldrons and report on washing.

sentences.zh: 祀官御史省饌具，乃還齋所。

translations.literal: Sacrificial officers and censors inspect the food offerings, then return to the purification quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial officers and censors inspect the food offerings, then return to the purification quarters.

sentences.zh: 祀日，未明十五刻，太官令帥宰人以鸞刀割牲，祝史以豆取毛血，各置於饌所，遂烹牲。

translations.literal: On the sacrifice day, at the fifteenth quarter before dawn, the Imperial Kitchen Director leads butchers to cut the victims with the imperial knife; invokers take blood and hair in dou vessels, each placed at the food station, and the victims are then cooked.
translations.idiomatic: On the sacrifice day, at the fifteenth quarter before dawn, the Imperial Kitchen Director leads butchers to cut the victims with the imperial knife. invokers take blood and hair in dou vessels, each placed at the food station, and the victims are then cooked.

sentences.zh: 其于廟亦如之。

translations.literal: At the temple it is likewise.

sentences.zh: 皇帝詣罍洗，侍中跪取匜，興，沃水；

translations.literal: " Those in position all bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: " Those in position all bow twice.

sentences.zh: 又跪取盤，興，承水。

translations.literal: The emperor proceeds to the urn wash; the attendant-in-chief kneels, takes the pitcher, rises, and pours water;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor proceeds to the urn wash. the attendant-in-chief kneels, takes the pitcher, rises, and pours water;

sentences.zh: 皇帝搢珪，盥手。

translations.literal: again kneels, takes the basin, rises, and receives the water.
translations.idiomatic: again kneels. takes the basin, rises, and receives the water.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎跪取巾於篚；

translations.literal: rises, receives the cloth with the wrapper, kneels and places it in the basket.
translations.idiomatic: He rises, receives the cloth with the wrapper, kneels, and places it in the basket.

sentences.zh: 興，以帨受巾，跪奠於篚。

translations.literal: rises, receives the cloth with the wrapper, kneels and places it in the basket.
translations.idiomatic: He rises, receives the cloth with the wrapper, kneels, and places it in the basket.

sentences.zh: 又取瓚於篚，興，以進，皇帝受瓚。

translations.literal: Again takes the libation cup from the basket, rises, and advances; the emperor receives the cup.
translations.idiomatic: Again he took the libation cup from the basket, rose, and advanced; the emperor received the cup.

sentences.zh: 侍中酌水奉盤，皇帝洗瓚，黃門侍郎授巾如初。

translations.literal: The attendant-in-chief pours water and presents the basin; the emperor washes the cup; the Vice Director of the Yellow Gate hands the cloth as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant-in-chief poured water and presented the basin; the emperor washed the cup, and the Vice Director of the Yellow Gate handed the cloth as before.

sentences.zh: 皇帝拭瓚，升自阼階，就獻祖尊彝所。

translations.literal: The attendant-in-chief pours water and presents the basin; the emperor washes the cup; the Vice Director of the Yellow Gate hands the cloth as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant-in-chief pours water and presents the basin; the Emperor washes the cup; the Vice Director of the Yellow Gate hands the cloth as at first.

sentences.zh: 執尊者舉冪，侍中贊酌鬱酒，進獻祖神座前，北向跪，以鬯祼地奠之，俛伏，興，少退，北向再拜。

translations.literal: The emperor wipes the cup, ascends the eastern steps, and goes to the Offering Ancestor's vessel position.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wipes the cup. ascends the eastern steps, and goes to the Offering Ancestor's vessel position.

sentences.zh: 又就懿祖尊彝所，執尊者舉冪，侍中取瓚於坫以進，皇帝受瓚。

translations.literal: The vessel-holder raises the cover; the attendant-in-chief presents fragrant wine, advancing before the Offering Ancestor's spirit seat, kneeling north, pouring the libation on the ground to present it, prostrating, rising, stepping back slightly, and bowing twice facing north.
translations.idiomatic: The vessel-holder raises the cover. the attendant-in-chief presents fragrant wine, advancing before the Offering Ancestor's spirit seat, kneeling north, pouring the libation on the ground to present it, prostrating, rising, stepping back slightly, and bowing twice facing north.

sentences.zh: 侍中贊酌鬱酒，進懿祖神座前，南向跪，以鬯祼地奠之。

translations.literal: Again at the Esteemed Ancestor's vessel position, the vessel-holder raises the cover; the attendant-in-chief takes the cup from the stand to advance; the emperor receives the cup.
translations.idiomatic: Again at the Esteemed Ancestor's vessel position, the vessel-holder raises the cover; the attendant-in-chief takes the cup from the stand to advance; the Emperor receives the cup.

sentences.zh: 次祼太祖以下，皆如懿祖。

translations.literal: The attendant-in-chief presents fragrant wine, advancing before the Esteemed Ancestor's spirit seat, kneeling south, pouring the libation on the ground to present it.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant-in-chief presents fragrant wine. advancing before the Esteemed Ancestor's spirit seat, kneeling south, pouring the libation on the ground to present it.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降自阼階，復于版位。

translations.literal: Next libation for the Great Ancestor downward, all as for the Esteemed Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Next libation for the Great Ancestor downward, all as for the Esteemed Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 初，羣官已再拜，祝史各奉毛、血及肝、膋之豆立於東門外，齋郎奉爐炭、蕭、稷、黍各立於其後，以次入自正門，升自太階。

translations.literal: The various Chief Invokers each received hair, blood, liver, and fat on the steps and advanced to present before the spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Invokers received the hair, blood, liver, and fat on the steps and presented them before the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝各迎取毛、血、肝、膋於階上，進奠於神座前。

translations.literal: The various Chief Invokers each received hair, blood, liver, and fat on the steps and advanced to present before the spirit seats.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Invokers received the hair, blood, liver, and fat on the steps and presented them before the spirit seats.

sentences.zh: 祝史退立於尊所，齋郎奉爐炭置於神座之左，其蕭、稷、黍各置於其下，降自阼階以出。

translations.literal: Invokers withdrew to stand at the vessel positions; purification youths placed furnace coals left of the spirit seats, with artemisia, millet, and glutinous millet each below them, descending the eastern steps to exit.
translations.idiomatic: The invokers withdrew to the vessel positions; purification youths set furnace coals left of the spirit seats, with artemisia, millet, and glutinous millet below, then descended the eastern steps to exit.

sentences.zh: 諸太祝取肝、膋燔於爐，還尊所。

translations.literal: The various Chief Invokers took liver and fat and burned them on the furnace, then returned to the vessel positions.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Invokers burned the liver and fat on the furnace, then returned to the vessel positions.
